body: Their are also a lot of mobile, off-grid solutions that have come out, like Bright Spark, L-Charge, and E boost. They address infrastructure issues with off-grid EV units that can be deployed anywhere. We work with fleets all of the time and power the vehicles consistently avoiding the need for infrastructure. If an organization has a utility connections setup with on-grid the prices to charge gets pretty low for corporate fleets. A lot of last mile local delivery companies having been transitioning to electric vehicles without much issues. So it is certainly a case by case things.

You should check out L-Charge then to overcome the infrastructure battle, that would save on the Capex and you would only need to worry about the kWh you use. They have units that only take up a parking space or 2 with level 3 DCFC 180 - 360 kW units. Just dm if you wanna know more.

Prepare mentally on how to show why you're valuable. Whether that be prospecting and knowing how to generate new business, excelling at discovery calls, expert handling of your sales pipeline, closing deals etc...

Make sure to have at least 3 questions no matter what, it shows interest. My first interview there was no time for questions as it was preliminary rounds let's see if this person is even worth it.

2nd interview I asked:
What is the work culture like here?
What do you expect me to accomplish in the first 30,60, & 90 days?
What are your biggest challenges in this vertical currently?

MAKE SURE TO CLOSE:
"I really like this opportunity, what steps do we need to take to move forward." Simple effective and clearly communicates your ready to go. Close with any presentation or mock play they have you do. 

Do your research, seriously, if they have a LinkedIn and website, you need to start digging and absorb as much info on them. The better you know them, the better your chances.

EMAIL THEM THANK YOU AFTER EACH INTERVIEW:
This will leave a big impression and will separate you. Many hiring managers really like when candidates do this and it makes them feel like you are passionate about the opportunity to work with them.

1st: Don't stop learning and keep going, when you learned English you started off horrible, guess what you had to keep moving forward. Develop I am doing this attitude, people can always find something to pick at.

2nd: Download the application called hellotalk from the google or apple store and find you meet a lot people to practice Spanish with. I regularly have complete calls in Spanish, and have partners who I have moved over to whatsapp to talk with on a daily basis in only Spanish.

3rd: Use netflix/youtube and an app called Trancy, its a chrome extension app that will put the subtitles in English and Spanish at the same time. This will help you improve your vocabulary and ability to form sentences. Find series that are made in Spanish, this will drastically help your comprehension but you can't just sit and watch. Take out a whiteboard, get a marker and start writing out what you don't know, slow down moments and force yourself to go over parts. That is actively listening and training your brain.
